name: De Stijl
visualIdentity: Supplemental design reference, not a style directly named in the source collection. Uses aligned rectangles, horizontal and vertical rules, and connected color fields. Keep boundaries orthogonal and control line weight and area ratios.
suitableUses: Explicitly suited to rhythmic abstract and identity work. It can also support UI and product storytelling, editorial layouts, motion posters, staged geometric compositions, and short labels within color fields. These are inferred fits; use it when the grid serves the subject.
limitations: Avoid arbitrary diagonals, rounded corners, and gradients. Adapt or omit pinned or chaptered motion when it crops important details, forces text into unsafe areas, disrupts page layout, obscures causality, or adds unnecessary hierarchy changes. Keep data areas truthful and category counts within palette capacity.
palette: Use only red, yellow, blue, black, and white. Suggested tokens for new artwork are white #FFFFFF, black #000000, red #D02020, yellow #F4CB28, and blue #184BA0; these are suggestions, not canonical colors. Preserve supplied, brand, reference, semantic, and asset colors exactly. Keep fields discrete, with no gradients. Suggested opaque text pairs include black on white or yellow, and white on red or blue; check actual compositing and readability.
motionAndInteraction: Expand, divide, slide, or recolor rectangles while preserving orthogonal edges and connected fields. Favor authored, coherent movement but retain deliberate cuts, impacts, constant-speed passages, and reading holds; avoid elastic easing and unrelated effects. For video, use deterministic seekable composition time independent of live input. Interactive pages may map finite scroll progress to pinned-stage recomposition, reversible chapter handoffs, or story states; keep the outer pin stable, animate inner elements, and release without a jump. Support keyboard, touch, and reduced motion where applicable.
audio: No fixed soundtrack or required audio layer is specified. Choose music, voiceover, vocals, effects, ambience, or silence for the topic and audience; honor supplied assets and explicit requirements. Keep speech intelligible and synchronized, avoid clipping or competing vocals, and inspect sound with picture.
assetRequirements: Use task-provided assets and exact copy. No specific assets are prescribed. For HTML, SVG can draw scalable rectangles, strokes, masks, and clipping paths; load local fonts and assets. Optional diagram assets may be exported in layers if separately animated. Do not recolor approved artwork.
combinations: Works alone for rhythmic abstract and identity pieces. Inferred compatible hybrids include proportional rectangle-area data displays with style-097, using no more than three categories for red/yellow/blue and labels only on white cells, and orthogonal block-sans labels with style-093, keeping text within cells and lines constant. Avoid unsupported category counts or misleading area scaling.
productionApproach: Choose drawing and motion methods for the visual requirements first; SVG is recommended for rendering and GSAP for deterministic, seekable motion. HyperFrames is the primary video assembly, timing, synchronization, validation, and export pipeline. Use Remotion only if HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation blocks a required capability, and record why. For interactive HTML, scroll can drive progress; video must not depend on live scrolling. Assign one owner per animated property, inspect key states and final output, and state unverified limitations.
